facts.fact: Access Now says Algeria's Education Minister Mohamed Seghir Saadaoui explained connectivity would be imposed only inside exam centres from the Baccalaureate start on 7 June 2026.

Amnesty International says Algerian authorities have detained, prosecuted or convicted seven journalists and media workers since November 2025 over their work or opinions, including journalist Hassan Bouras held in pretrial detention since 12 April 2026.

Amnesty International says an Algerian court sentenced the director of the online channel Vision TV to a suspended one-year term and ordered the channel closed and its equipment seized, after journalist Saad Bouakba was convicted on 4 December 2025 over an interview given to it.

note: Describes new speech offences promulgated 5 May 2024 with no person reported charged under them, no cut and no repeal.

facts.fact: Committee for Justice reports that on 7 July 2026 the Algiers appeal court confirmed journalist Saad Bouakba's guilt for statements on historical events, reducing his sentence to 18 months suspended and a fine of one million dinars.

note: The definitive closure of the online outlet Rassd is stated without a date or the reason, so no fact is recorded for it.

facts.fact: TSA Algerie reports that on the first baccalaureate day, 15 June 2025, social networks including Facebook and TikTok were blocked in Algeria though there was no general internet cut, and the education minister said cutting the internet is a tool to prevent exam fraud.
Global Voices says Algeria has cut the national internet every year during the baccalaureate exams.

note: Document states nothing the study asks.
